notes.text: Page-wide controls always on screen: the GUI control should be fixed so that variants can be toggled on different previews anywhere on the page for better back-and-forth comparisons.
Pixel-perfect previews: the iframe previews throw off anything related to size; never zoom, scale or transform a specimen whose size is being judged.
More real UI: live production components and whole real pages as the comparison surfaces, not a screen of specimens.
The app's UI is open: any UI that touches the app in an active lab track may be worked on before the dedicated app agents get to it later.
Dark and light are chosen separately; dark applies to marketing and the app's dark mode, light to paper and the app's light mode. Argue the theming model from the ground up.
Feels like a research report without applicable takeaways; synthesise the spill doctrine and placements into it; the section configurator for aurora placements is the promising part.
Show the voices in use on production UI across marketing and the app; every comparison must show the distinction.
Pivot to discovery and sourcing: a few potential sources rather than exact picks.

A question carries its context: on the desk it was tough to understand what was being asked for most of the questions; very technical terms and nicknames from spots in the boards force a reader deep into the track to gain the context to even begin understanding the question. Having the link helps a bit, but framing the context with the question would help a ton. The more clearly a question is asked, the more easily it is answered.

Each exploration page feels like a small research paper into its track. The goal is to get creative while designing to find a combination of intuitive content flow and layouts and engaging visuals: a few of our best concepts created for review, pick the best direction and refine for production polish. Designing a few (or many, complexity and context dependent) variations always beats a mountain of research text.

Reads like a PhD on color theory when we are simply exploring new palettes; six configs that are not clearly explained, toggled around the page to see what they impact. A dozen polished variants with preview palettes and some demo UI to configure and compare would have been far more helpful: build explorations as a catalog of previews to select from.
